title: Count sheets, not just rolls
hook: Six rolls or four rolls? The count inside each roll changes the arithmetic.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate the usable unit count inside multipacks before comparing prices.

misconception: More rolls necessarily means more usable paper.
objective: Calculate the usable unit count inside multipacks before comparing prices.

claims.text: A costs €6: six rolls of 120 sheets. B costs €5: four rolls of 240 sheets. Scaled model; identical sheet size; fictional prices.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Sheets/roll=240, A=0.008€/sheet and B=0.005€/sheet. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",6,["*",6,120]]; B=["/",5,["*",4,"x"]]; x denotes Sheets/roll. At x=240, A=0.00833333333333, B=0.00520833333333. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The denominator is total sheets: rolls multiplied by sheets per roll. Comparing only roll counts hides the usable quantity. This model assumes equal sheet size and quality.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",6,["*",6,120]]; B=["/",5,["*",4,"x"]]; x denotes Sheets/roll. At x=240, A=0.00833333333333, B=0.00520833333333. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Fictional packs: eight rolls of 150 sheets for €6, or four rolls of 300 sheets for €5. Which costs less per sheet? Correct: The four-roll pack. Both packs hold 1,200 sheets (rolls × sheets per roll), so the €5 pack costs less per sheet; the roll count hid that.

claims.text: A unit price expresses cost per stated quantity; comparable unit-price labels use consistent units of measure.
claims.source: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/1181e2025/NIST.SP.1181e2025.html NIST SP 1181-2025, Definitions / Unit Pricing and E-Commerce. Opened 2026-10-13. Dataset prices and package amounts are invented for the arithmetic demonstration.

claims.text: Six rolls or four rolls? The count inside each roll changes the arithmetic.
claims.source: Hook (meta.json hook; resource-specs.json "lh-count-sheets-not-rolls".hook), recorded as a claim per FC LH-1 "Hooks with no claim (25)" (W-367, 2026-10-14, demo-builder). Follows from this lesson's declared expressions in src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json, evaluated by resource-model.ts: A (Six-rolls)=["/", 6, ["*", 6, 120]]; B (Four-rolls)=["/", 5, ["*", 4, "x"]]; x denotes Sheets/roll, 100 to 300, start 240. FC LH-4 (2026-10-14, fact-checker, W-380): verified (hook): A = 6/(6×120) = €0.00833/sheet; B = 5/(4x): €0.0125 at 100, equal at 150, €0.0052 at 240; which pack is cheaper per sheet flips with sheets per roll, so the count inside each roll changes the result.
